recognize_zh: 低倍視野中大量紅血球內含細小的環狀或點狀寄生蟲，常一個紅血球內有多個，另見紅血球外的小型蟲體，且沒有瘧色素、裂殖體或配子體，符合巴貝西蟲（Babesia）高寄生率感染。
features: Numerous red cells containing tiny intraerythrocytic ring, dot and pear-shaped forms
Multiple parasites within single red cells in many cells, indicating high parasitemia
Small extracellular parasite forms scattered between red cells (some dots may represent platelets)
No hemozoin pigment, schizonts or gametocytes; infected red cells not enlarged
Tetrad (Maltese cross) forms not resolvable at this magnification
Single neutrophil (band/segmented) in the center of the field
describe_en: Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smear, photographed at low magnification through the eyepiece, shows a high proportion of red cells containing tiny intraerythrocytic ring, dot and pyriform organisms, frequently several within a single red cell. Small extracellular forms are scattered between red cells, although some of these dots could represent platelets. Infected red cells are not enlarged, and there is no hemozoin pigment, schizonts or gametocytes; tetrad forms cannot be resolved at this power. A single neutrophil is present. Findings are consistent with Babesia infection with high parasitemia; confirmation by high-power review for tetrads and PCR is recommended.

ddx.vs: P. falciparum also shows multiple small rings per red cell but lacks extracellular forms and tetrads and may show banana-shaped gametocytes, Maurer's clefts or pigment.
Superimposed platelets are granular, often surrounded by a halo and lie in a different focal plane, rather than forming delicate rings with a pale center.
Howell-Jolly bodies are single, solid, round nuclear remnants and Pappenheimer bodies are clustered peripheral granules, neither forming rings or multiple pyriform forms.
Precipitate lies on top of cells and background in varied focal planes and lacks the consistent ring morphology of parasites.
